A critical breakthrough occurred when the CF3 group was replaced with a cyano group, significantly improving the score to 0.471. Further optimization revealed that combining a cyano group with one hydroxyl and one methoxy substituent on the phenyl ring yielded 0.483.

Systematic exploration of N-substituents showed that bulkier groups improved activity: N-isopropyl (0.500) < N-tert-butyl (0.501). The optimal benzimidazole substitution was achieved by replacing fluorine with methyl, reaching the highest score of **0.507**.
